definition_zh: 依靠；依赖；取决于
definition_en: to need someone or something for support or success
core_image: 垂下的枝条紧抓着支架才不倒下
scene: 运动会上，接力赛成绩和队友配合有关。 Our relay team will depend on every runner doing their best.
sceneCN: 这里 depend 是「取决于」（第 2 个义项：结果由某事决定）；句意是我们接力队能否取胜取决于每个人尽全力。

derivatives.zh: 由 depend 加名词后缀 -ence 构成，义为「依赖；依靠」
由 depend 加形容词后缀 -ent 构成，义为「依赖的；取决于…的」
由 in-（不）加 dependent 构成，义为「独立的」
由 sus-（下）加 pend（悬挂）构成，义为「悬挂；暂停」

senses.title: To need someone or something
senses.definition: to need the help or support of someone or something
senses.definitionCN: 需要某人或某物的帮助与支持
senses.example: The little cat still depends on its mother for food.
senses.exampleCN: 小猫还得靠猫妈妈喂食。
senses.why: To hang from something is to be held up by it, so needing support keeps the hanging image.
senses.whyCN: 「挂」在东西上就是被它撑着，需要支撑便保留了悬挂的画面。

senses.title: To be decided by something
senses.definition: to be controlled or decided by something else
senses.definitionCN: 由别的事物决定或控制
senses.example: Whether we have the match depends on the weather.
senses.exampleCN: 比赛是否举行取决于天气。
senses.why: A hanging thing moves with what holds it, so outcomes hang on their causes.
senses.whyCN: 悬挂之物随支点而动，结果便「挂」在原因上，随原因而定。

senses.title: To trust someone
senses.definition: to trust that someone will do what is needed
senses.definitionCN: 相信某人会做到所需之事
senses.example: You can depend on Li Ming to bring the ball.
senses.exampleCN: 你可以相信李明会把球带来。
senses.why: Trusting is leaning on a person, resting your weight on their promise.
senses.whyCN: 信任就是把自己「靠」在一个人身上，把重量放在他的承诺上。

intro.en: Depend comes from Latin words for hanging down.
intro.cn: depend 来自拉丁语中表示「垂下、悬挂」的词。

items.en: Dependere meant to hang down or hang from, from de- plus pendere (to hang).
items.cn: 拉丁语 dependere 意为垂下、挂于，由 de- 加 pendere（悬挂）构成。

items.en: French kept dependre for hanging things.
items.cn: 法语保留 dependre 表示悬挂。

items.en: English took depend in the fifteenth century, first for physical hanging.
items.cn: 英语在十五世纪吸收 depend，最初指实际的悬挂。

items.en: The meaning moved to needing support, then to being decided by something.
items.cn: 词义转到「需要支撑」，再转到「由某事决定」。

items.en: It depends became a common answer meaning the case decides.
items.cn: It depends 成了常用回答，意为「看情况而定」。

note.en: These words share the hanging root or describe reliance.
note.cn: 这些词与「悬挂」词根同源，或同样描述依靠关系。

normalIntro.cn: 用「悬挂」的画面和 pend 词族记住 depend。

normal.cn: de-（向下）加 pend（悬挂）：挂在下面。

normal.cn: 固定搭配是 depend on（依靠）。

normal.en: It depends is a handy answer.

normal.en: independent starts with in-, meaning not depending.
normal.cn: independent 以 in- 开头，表示不依赖。

abstract.en: Picture a swing hanging from a strong branch.
abstract.cn: 想象秋千挂在结实的树枝上。

abstract.en: Feel a baby bird waiting for its parent.
abstract.cn: 体会雏鸟等待亲鸟喂食的心情。

abstract.en: Hear a coach say the result depends on your training.
abstract.cn: 听教练说结果取决于你的训练。

examples.en: Young children depend on adults for food and safety.
examples.cn: 幼儿在饮食和安全上都依靠大人。

examples.en: The picnic depends on tomorrow's weather.
examples.cn: 野餐能不能成要看明天的天气。

examples.en: In team games, you depend on your teammates too.
examples.cn: 在团队比赛中，你也要依靠队友。

definition_zh: 背景；出身；背景情况
definition_en: the part behind the main thing, or a person's family and training, or facts that explain something
core_image: 照片里人物背后连绵的群山
scene: 照片里，人物背后是连绵的群山。 The mountains form the background of the photo.
sceneCN: 这里 background 是「背景」（第 1 个义项：画面主体后面的部分）；句意为群山构成照片的背景。

pos.zh: 名词：背景；出身；背景情况

derivatives.zh: 向后
地面
背景（复数）

senses.title: The part behind the subject
senses.definition: the part of a picture or a scene that lies behind the main thing
senses.definitionCN: 图画或场景中位于主体后面的部分
senses.example: The mountains form the background of the photo.
senses.exampleCN: 群山构成照片的背景。
senses.why: The ground behind the subject is literally the back ground of the picture, which is the first sense.
senses.whyCN: 主体后面的那片地面就是画面的「后景」，这是第一义。

senses.title: A person's origin
senses.definition: a person's family, education and earlier life
senses.definitionCN: 一个人的家庭、教育与早年经历
senses.example: She comes from a farming background.
senses.exampleCN: 她出身于务农家庭。
senses.why: A life also has a ground behind the present, and that earlier ground is called its background.
senses.whyCN: 人生也有位于当下之后的地面，那片更早的地面就叫背景。

senses.title: Facts that explain
senses.definition: facts and events that help explain something
senses.definitionCN: 有助于解释某事的事实与经过
senses.example: The teacher explained the background of the war.
senses.exampleCN: 老师讲解了这场战争的背景。
senses.why: What stands behind an event helps it make sense, which gives the sense of background information.
senses.whyCN: 站在事件后面的东西帮助人理解它，于是有「背景资料」的义项。

intro.en: The recorded history of background is set out below; the deeper origin is marked where it is uncertain.
intro.cn: 下面是 background 有记录的历史；更早的来源存疑处已作标注。

items.en: Bæc meant the back or the rear side.
items.cn: bæc 意为背部或后侧。

items.en: Grund meant the ground or the bottom.
items.cn: grund 意为地面或底部。

items.en: English joined back and ground into one noun.
items.cn: 英语把 back 与 ground 合成一个名词。

items.en: The word first named the ground behind a painted subject.
items.cn: 这个词最初指绘画主体后面的地面。

items.en: Today it also covers a person's origin and explaining facts.
items.cn: 今天它也涵盖一个人的出身与说明性的事实。

note.en: The first group collects forms that look or sound alike; the second group collects words with a nearby meaning.
note.cn: 第一组收形近或音近的词，第二组收意义相近的词。

entries.definitionCN: 事件周围的地点与条件。

entries.definition: The facts around something that give it meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 赋予某事意义的周边事实。

entries.definition: The earlier events that lead to the present.

normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用有记录的词形、真实的词族和这个词实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: back means behind and ground means the surface: background is the ground behind the main subject.
normal.cn: back 表示在后方，ground 表示地面：background 就是主体后面的那片地面。

normal.en: The same family also gives back and ground.
normal.cn: 同一词族还给出 back 与 ground。

normal.en: It often appears in the phrase in the background.
normal.cn: 它常出现在「在背景里」这个搭配里。

normal.en: Spell it as it sounds: keep every letter of background in order.
normal.cn: 按读音拼写：把 background 的每个字母按顺序保留。

normal.en: Use it when you mean: the part behind the main thing, or a person's family and training, or facts that explain something.
normal.cn: 当你想表达「背景」时用它。

abstract.en: Say the word aloud first, then let the picture bring the meaning back.
abstract.cn: 先把这个词读出声，再让画面把意思带回来。

definition_zh: 铁；熨斗；熨烫；链条（复数）
definition_en: a strong grey metal, a heated tool for smoothing cloth, or the act of pressing clothes with it
core_image: 一块灰黑色的金属锭，旁边放着一台还冒着蒸汽的熨斗
scene: 洗衣房里蒸汽升起，她左手扶着衬衫，右手推着沉重的熨斗走过领口。 The old gate is made of iron and has never rusted.
sceneCN: 这里 iron 是「铁」（第 1 个义项：那种金属），句意为这扇老门是铁做的，从来没有生锈。画面里的物件：熨斗、衬衫、蒸汽。

collocations.phrase: strike while the iron is hot

senses.title: The metal
senses.definition: a hard grey metal used for tools, rails, and gates
senses.definitionCN: 一种坚硬灰暗的金属，用于工具、铁轨与大门
senses.example: The bridge was built with iron beams from the old mill.
senses.exampleCN: 这座桥用了旧磨坊拆下来的铁梁。
senses.why: The metal sense is the oldest and stays attached to beams, rails, and gates.
senses.whyCN: 金属义最古老，至今仍与梁、轨、门连在一起。

senses.title: The smoothing tool
senses.definition: a flat heated tool used to press wrinkles out of cloth
senses.definitionCN: 一种扁平且加热的工具，用来压平布上的皱褶
senses.example: The iron was still hot when she put it down.
senses.exampleCN: 她放下熨斗时它还是烫的。
senses.why: The tool took the metal name because it was a block of iron heated over a fire.
senses.whyCN: 这个工具之所以借了金属的名字，因为它本是放在火上加热的铁块。

senses.title: Pressing clothes smooth
senses.definition: to press cloth with heat so that it lies flat
senses.definitionCN: 用热量压平布料
senses.example: He ironed his shirt five minutes before the interview.
senses.exampleCN: 面试前五分钟他才把衬衫熨好。
senses.why: The verb is simply the tool turned into an action.
senses.whyCN: 动词义就是把工具名直接变成动作。

senses.title: Chains and firm will
senses.definition: metal restraints, or metaphorically a hard and unyielding quality
senses.definitionCN: 金属镣铐，或比喻坚硬不屈的性质
senses.example: They spoke of the iron discipline of the mountain rescue team.
senses.exampleCN: 他们谈起山地救援队那种铁一般的纪律。
senses.why: From chains to character, the hard metal became a figure for what will not bend.
senses.whyCN: 从镣铐到性格，这种硬金属成了「不肯弯」的象征。

intro.en: Iron is an old Germanic word; its distant origin is uncertain, though Celtic is a strong candidate.
intro.cn: iron 是个古老的日耳曼词，更远的来源不确定，凯尔特语是较有力的候选。

items.en: The word appears as isern or iren in early texts.
items.cn: 这个词在早期文献中写作 isern 或 iren。

items.en: Related forms include German Eisen and Old Saxon isarn.
items.cn: 同源形式包括德语 Eisen 与古撒克逊语 isarn。

items.en: The deeper root may come from a Celtic metal word, but it is disputed.
items.cn: 更深层词根可能来自凯尔特语的金属词，但仍有争议。

items.en: Middle English changed the -s- to -r-, giving iren.
items.cn: 中古英语把 -s- 变成 -r-，写作 iren。

items.en: Modern English settled on iron for both the metal and the tool.
items.cn: 现代英语把 iron 固定下来，兼指金属与熨斗。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the iron spelling; the near-meaning group holds words for metals and pressing.
note.cn: 形近组共用 iron 拼写；近义组收表示金属与压平动作的词。

entries.definitionCN: 名词义为复数，也可指镣铐。

entries.definition: To make a surface even.

normalIntro.en: These hooks tie together the metal, the tool, and the act of pressing.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子把金属、工具和压平这个动作串起来。

normal.en: One word, one metal, one heavy tool.
normal.cn: 一个词，既是金属，也是那件沉工具。

normal.en: An iron is heavy because it is iron.
normal.cn: 熨斗沉，正是因为它就是铁。

normal.en: To iron is to press with that weight.
normal.cn: iron 作动词就是拿这份重量去压。

normal.en: German Eisen is a cousin from the same family.
normal.cn: 德语 Eisen 是同族的表亲。

normal.en: The -r- came late; early English said isern.
normal.cn: 那个 -r- 是后来才有，早先英语说 isern。

abstract.en: Iron is a metal that remembers the shape you give it.
abstract.cn: 铁是会记住你所给形状的金属。

abstract.en: An iron is iron made gentle by heat.
abstract.cn: 熨斗是被热软化过的铁。

abstract.en: Iron will is the metal kept uncooled.
abstract.cn: 铁一般的意志，是不肯冷却的金属。

examples.en: The locket is silver, but the chain is iron.
examples.cn: 坠子是银的，链子却是铁的。

examples.en: She ironed the curtains before hanging them again.
examples.cn: 她先把窗帘熨好再重新挂上。

examples.en: The prisoners wore irons on their ankles.
examples.cn: 囚犯脚踝上带着镣铐。

core.cn: 核心意象：一块沉得足以把布压平的灰色金属。

branches.cn: 铁梁这条线：被弯成桥梁与大门的金属。

branches.cn: 工具这条线：同一块金属加上把手和热。

branches.en: THE ACT: pressing cloth until wrinkles go.
branches.cn: 动作这条线：把布压到皱褶消失。

branches.cn: 手这条线：工具和动作本是同一个意思。

definition_zh: 新闻；消息；新闻报道；新闻节目
definition_en: information about recent events, especially as reported by newspapers, radio or television
core_image: 一叠刚送到门口的消息，油墨还没凉
scene: 清晨的广播刚响，主播念出第一条消息，厨房里的人立刻停下手里的活。 The news spread through the village before noon.
sceneCN: 这里 news 是「消息、新闻」（第 1 个义项：关于近期发生之事的信息）；句意为消息在中午之前就传遍了村子。图中可辨识物件：广播喇叭、餐桌上的早餐碗。

derivatives.zh: news 加 -y，义为「消息多的；爱说闲话的」
由 news 与 worthy 复合，义为「有新闻价值的」
由 news 与 paper 复合，义为「报纸」
由 news 与 letter 复合，义为「通讯；简报」

senses.title: Information about recent events
senses.definition: facts or information about something that has happened recently
senses.definitionCN: 关于最近发生的事情的事实或信息
senses.example: The news of the rescue reached us by radio.
senses.exampleCN: 救援的消息通过广播传到了我们这里。
senses.why: News began as the plural of new, so it first names fresh things gathered together and told to someone else.
senses.whyCN: news 起初是 new 的复数，所以它最初指的是把一件件新鲜事收拢在一起，再讲给别人听。

senses.title: Reports of current events
senses.definition: reports of recent events printed in papers or broadcast on radio and television
senses.definitionCN: 刊登在报纸上或通过广播电视播出的近期事件报道
senses.example: The evening news covered the flood in three villages.
senses.exampleCN: 晚间新闻报道了三个村庄的洪水。
senses.why: Once fresh things are collected and published, the word moves from the information itself to the work of reporting it.
senses.whyCN: 新鲜事一旦被收集并刊播，词义就从「信息本身」转到「报道这项工作」上。

senses.title: A news programme
senses.definition: a regular television or radio programme that reports recent events
senses.definitionCN: 定期播出、报道近期事件的电视或广播节目
senses.example: She watches the news every night before bed.
senses.exampleCN: 她每晚睡前都看新闻节目。
senses.why: The same word can name the half hour on the screen because that slot is filled with nothing but collected news.
senses.whyCN: 同一个词也能指屏幕上那半小时，因为那个时段里装的正是收集起来的新闻。

senses.title: Something worth reporting
senses.titleCN: 值得报道的事；新闻素材
senses.definition: a person or event interesting enough to be reported as news
senses.definitionCN: 足够有趣、值得当作新闻来报道的人或事
senses.example: A cat stuck on a roof was the news of the week.
senses.exampleCN: 一只猫被困在屋顶上，成了本周的新闻。
senses.why: When the telling matters more than the event, the word shifts again to mean whatever supplies the story.
senses.whyCN: 当「讲出去」比「发生了什么」更重要时，词义再次偏移，转而指任何能提供故事的材料。

intro.en: News was originally the plural of the adjective new, meaning new things; the spelling and its singular, uncountable use settled in the early modern period.
intro.cn: news 原本是形容词 new 的复数，意为「新事物」；它的拼写以及单数、不可数的用法在近代早期固定下来。

items.en: The adjective nīwe meant new and could also stand as a noun for a new thing.
items.cn: 形容词 nīwe 意为「新的」，也可当名词用，指一件新事物。

items.en: Middle English used newes, the plural of new, for new things or fresh reports.
items.cn: 中古英语用 newes，即 new 的复数，指新事物或新得到的消息。

items.en: The spelling settled as news, and the word was increasingly treated as a singular mass noun.
items.cn: 拼写固定为 news，并越来越被当作不可数的单数名词使用。

items.en: News became the everyday word for printed reports and was combined with paper to form newspaper.
items.cn: news 成为印刷报道的常用词，并与 paper 组合成 newspaper。

items.en: Modern English keeps news uncountable and uses it for media reports, broadcasts and phrases such as good news.
items.cn: 现代英语让 news 保持不可数，用它指媒体报道、广播节目，以及 good news 这类说法。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on new or on the news compound; the near-meaning group gathers words for information and reports.
note.cn: 形近组收以 new 或 news 复合而成的词；近义组收表示信息与报道的词。

entries.definition: Recently made; the adjective from which news was formed.
entries.definitionCN: 新近制成的；news 正是由它构成。

entries.definition: Printed sheets that carry news.
entries.definitionCN: 承载新闻的印刷纸张；报纸。

entries.definition: A radio or television broadcast of news.
entries.definitionCN: 广播或电视的新闻播报。

entries.definition: Full of news or gossip.
Facts told or learned about something.
entries.definitionCN: 被告知或了解到的关于某事的事实。

entries.definition: A spoken or written account of an event.
entries.definitionCN: 对事件的口头或书面叙述。

entries.definition: A short official statement or news update.
entries.definitionCN: 简短的官方公告或新闻更新。

entries.definition: Old-fashioned word for news.
entries.definitionCN: 消息；旧时或书面语的说法。

normalIntro.en: The word grew out of new as a bundle of fresh things, and its family keeps connecting freshness, reporting and the media that carry it.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词从 new 长出来，本是一捆新鲜事；词族始终把新鲜、报道与承载报道的媒体连在一起。

normal.en: news is new plus a plural s: a bundle of new things told to others.
normal.cn: news 是 new 加复数词尾 s：把一捆新鲜事讲给别人听。

normal.en: It looks plural but takes a singular verb: the news is good.
normal.cn: 它看起来像复数，却接单数动词：the news is good。

normal.en: There is no a news; say a piece of news or a news item.
normal.cn: 不能说 a news，要说 a piece of news 或 a news item。

normal.en: Common compounds include newspaper, newscast, newsstand and newsletter.
normal.cn: 常见复合词包括 newspaper、newscast、newsstand 与 newsletter。

normal.en: Good news and bad news both stay uncountable and never take a plural verb.
normal.cn: good news 与 bad news 都保持不可数，也从不接复数动词。

abstract.en: A mass of fresh facts becomes a single uncountable word because the telling, not the counting, is what matters.
abstract.cn: 一堆新鲜事实变成一个不可数词，因为重要的是「讲出去」，而不是「数清楚」。

abstract.en: The same word can be the story, the printed page and the evening programme, because all three are ways of carrying a report.
abstract.cn: 同一个词可以指故事、印出的纸页和晚间节目，因为三者都是承载报道的方式。

abstract.en: News is freshness organised until it can travel.
abstract.cn: news 就是被整理到可以传播为止的新鲜。

examples.en: The news spread through the village before noon.
examples.cn: 消息在中午之前就传遍了村子。

examples.en: I have good news for you: the scholarship is yours.
examples.cn: 我有好消息告诉你：奖学金归你了。

examples.en: She listens to the news on the radio while cooking.
examples.cn: 她做饭时听广播里的新闻。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「纽斯」——「纽斯」是新事的声音；一条条新事凑起来，就成了新闻。

root: 中古英语 newes 是 new 的复数，本义「新的事物、新消息」；后拼作 news，被当作不可数名词。与拉丁语 novus（新）同出原始印欧语词根。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is fresh information; the senses then divide into the reports, the broadcast programme and whatever is worth reporting.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是新鲜的信息；义项由此分出报道、广播节目，以及任何值得报道的材料。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stack of fresh reports arriving at the door, still warm from the press.
core.cn: 核心意象：一叠刚送到门口的消息，油墨还没凉。

branches.en: a neighbour telling you what happened last night
branches.cn: 邻居告诉你昨晚发生了什么

branches.en: a front page filled with the flood
branches.cn: 登满洪水的头版

branches.en: a family sitting before the evening broadcast
branches.cn: 一家人坐在晚间节目前的样子

branches.en: a cat on a roof drawing a crowd
branches.cn: 屋顶上的猫引来一群人

branches.en: one word for the story, the paper and the programme
branches.cn: 同一个词，兼指故事、报纸与节目

intro.en: The word is new plus a plural ending, and its compounds pair that root with the things that carry reports.
intro.cn: 这个词是 new 加一个复数词尾，它的复合词把这个词根与承载报道的事物配在一起。

latinIntro.en: Latin novus is a distant cousin through the same reconstructed root for new, not a direct source of the English word.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 novus 通过同一个重构的「新」词根与它远亲相连，并不是这个英语词的直接来源。

definition_zh: 大的；大型的；大量的；广泛的
definition_en: big in size, amount or importance, or broad in range
core_image: 一双手在身前比出一个很宽的圆，几乎抱不过来
scene: 仓库门被推开，里面堆着一人多高的木箱。 A large shipment of rice arrived at the port.
sceneCN: 这里是「大量的、大批的」（第 2 个义项：指数量或规模大）；句意为一大批大米运抵港口。图中可辨识物件：仓库门、堆叠的木箱、货运单。

derivatives.zh: 由 large 加 -ly 构成，义为「大部分；主要地」
由 en- 加 large 构成，义为「扩大；放大」
由 large 经法语 largesse 而来，义为「慷慨；施赠」
由 large 加 -ish 构成，义为「相当大的」

senses.title: Big in physical size
senses.definition: big in size or dimensions compared with others of the same kind
senses.definitionCN: 与同类相比在尺寸或体积上很大
senses.example: They moved into a large house near the river.
senses.exampleCN: 他们搬进了河边一栋大房子。
senses.why: Large came from a Latin word for abundance, so its first English sense is simply 'much in size'.
senses.whyCN: large 来自一个表示「丰足」的拉丁词，所以它最早在英语里就是「尺寸上很大」。

senses.title: Great in amount or scale
senses.definition: great in number, amount or extent, as in a large shipment or a large sum
senses.definitionCN: 在数量、金额或规模上很大，如大批货物或大笔款项
senses.example: A large shipment of rice arrived at the port.
senses.exampleCN: 一大批大米运抵港口。
senses.why: From size the word moves easily to amount: what takes up much space often also comes in great quantity.
senses.whyCN: 从体积很容易转到数量：占地方多的东西，往往数量也大。

senses.title: Broad in range or importance
senses.definition: wide in scope, importance or influence rather than in physical size
senses.definitionCN: 在范围、重要性或影响上广，而不是体积大
senses.example: The decision has a large effect on small businesses.
senses.exampleCN: 这项决定对小企业有重大影响。
senses.why: A wide circle is also a wide reach, so large extends from space to influence and significance.
senses.whyCN: 一个很大的圆也是很大的覆盖范围，于是 large 从空间扩展到影响与重要性。

senses.title: Not confined; at liberty
senses.definition: free from confinement, especially in the fixed phrase at large
senses.definitionCN: 不受拘禁，尤用于固定说法 at large
senses.example: The escaped prisoner is still at large.
senses.exampleCN: 那名逃犯仍在逃。
senses.why: At large once meant 'at liberty, without limits'; the phrase keeps the old sense of a space with no walls.
senses.whyCN: at large 早先意为「自由、没有限制」，这个短语保留了「没有围墙的空间」这一旧义。

intro.en: Large came into English through French from a Latin word meaning abundant and generous, and it kept both size and generosity for a while.
intro.cn: large 经法语进入英语，源头是意为「丰足、慷慨」的拉丁词，曾同时保留「大」与「慷慨」两层意思。

items.en: Largus meant abundant, plentiful and generous, a word about giving much rather than about size alone.
items.cn: largus 意为丰足的、充裕的、慷慨的，重点在「给得多」，而不只是尺寸。

items.en: Old French large kept the sense of wide, generous and abundant.
items.cn: 古法语 large 保留宽广、慷慨、丰足的意思。

items.en: Middle English large covers breadth, generosity and physical size at once.
items.cn: 中古英语的 large 同时覆盖宽广、慷慨与体积大。

items.en: By the fourteenth century the everyday sense of big in size is firmly established.
items.cn: 到十四世纪，「尺寸大」的日常义已经稳固确立。

items.en: Modern English keeps the size sense and preserves the older freedom sense in at large.
items.cn: 现代英语保留尺寸义，并在 at large 中保存了较早的「自由」义。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the same stem; the near-meaning group gathers size words from big to enormous.
note.cn: 形近组收同一词干构成的词；近义组收从 big 到 enormous 的尺寸词。

entries.definition: Mostly, or to a great extent.
To make or become bigger.
Generous giving of money or gifts.
Fairly large.
Of great size, the most general word.
Extremely large.
Covering a large area or range.
Large in amount or importance.

normalIntro.en: The word is short but its family is wide, and the old sense of generosity still hides in one phrase.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词很短，但同族很广，古老的「慷慨」义还藏在一个短语里。

normal.en: Large takes -ly to become largely, meaning mostly.
normal.cn: large 加 -ly 成为 largely，意为「大部分」。

normal.en: Enlarge adds en- 'make' and means to make large.
normal.cn: enlarge 加 en-（使……），意为「使变大」。

normal.en: At large keeps an old sense: free, not confined.
normal.cn: at large 保留旧义：自由、不受拘束。

normal.en: Irregular comparison: large, larger, largest.
normal.cn: 不规则比较：large、larger、largest。

normal.en: By and large is a fixed phrase meaning 'generally speaking'.
normal.cn: by and large 是固定短语，意为「总的来说」。

abstract.en: A word born from generosity reminds us that size and giving were once the same idea.
abstract.cn: 一个从「慷慨」诞生的词提醒人：大小与给予曾是同一个观念。

abstract.en: Large measures space, amount and influence, three scales that rarely agree.
abstract.cn: large 同时衡量空间、数量与影响，这三种尺度很少一致。

abstract.en: At large shows how a phrase can keep an older meaning alive after the word itself has moved on.
abstract.cn: at large 说明短语能在词本身往前走之后，把旧义保存下来。

examples.en: They moved into a large house near the river.
examples.cn: 他们搬进了河边一栋大房子。

examples.en: A large shipment of rice arrived at the port.
examples.cn: 一大批大米运抵港口。

examples.en: The escaped prisoner is still at large.
examples.cn: 那名逃犯仍在逃。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「拉齐」——把东西拉齐排成一大片，就是 large。

root: 拉丁语 largus（丰足、慷慨）经古法语 large 进入英语；同族词多与「大、宽、给得多」有关。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a wide, abundant extent; it moves from physical size to amount, to influence, and finally to freedom from limits.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「宽而丰足的范围」；义项从体积转到数量，再到影响，最后到不受限制的自由。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two hands drawing a circle so wide that they can hardly reach around it.
core.cn: 核心意象：两只手在身前比出一个宽得几乎抱不过来的圆。

branches.en: a house that fills the width of the lane
branches.cn: 占满小巷宽度的大房子

branches.en: a shipment stacked higher than a person
branches.cn: 堆得比人还高的货物

branches.en: a decision that reaches every small shop
branches.cn: 影响每家小店的决策

branches.en: a prisoner with no walls around him
branches.cn: 身边没有围墙的囚犯

branches.en: size that becomes reach
branches.cn: 变成影响力的尺寸

intro.en: A Latin adjective of abundance, a French reshaping, and three English suffixes carry the family.
intro.cn: 一个表示丰足的拉丁形容词、一次法语改造，以及三个英语后缀支撑起这个词族。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

definition_zh: 颈；脖子；领口；（瓶、琴等的）细长颈部；地峡；拥吻
definition_en: the part of the body joining the head to the shoulders; a narrow joining part of an object; the opening of a garment; a narrow strip of land; and, informally, to kiss and hold someone closely
core_image: 一双手环绕在头与肩之间，把两端连成一条柔软的通道
scene: 入冬后风从领口灌进来，母亲把围巾绕过孩子颈后，又把垂下来的一端塞进外套。 She wrapped the scarf around the child's neck and tucked the loose end into his coat.
sceneCN: 这里「neck」是「脖子、颈部」（第 1 个义项：连接头与肩的身体部位）；句意是母亲把围巾绕在孩子脖子上，把垂下的一端塞进外套。图中可辨识物件：围巾、外套、被风掀起的领口。

pos.zh: 颈；脖子；领口；细长颈部；地峡

derivatives.zh: 由 neck 与 line 复合而成，义为「领口线；领口」
由 neck 与 lace 复合而成，义为「项链」
由 turtle 与 neck 复合而成，义为「高领；高领毛衣」

senses.title: The part joining the head to the body
senses.definition: the narrow part of the body that connects the head to the shoulders and chest
senses.definitionCN: 连接头部与肩胸之间那段较窄的身体部位
senses.example: The cat rubbed its neck against the door frame.
senses.exampleCN: 猫把脖子蹭在门框上。
senses.why: Old English hnecca named the narrow bridge between head and trunk; the shape of a constriction between two wider ends is what the word first points at.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 hnecca 指的就是头与躯干之间那条窄窄的桥；这个词最早指向的是「两端宽、中间收窄」的形状。

senses.title: A narrow joining part of an object
senses.definition: the long narrow part of an object, such as a bottle or a stringed instrument, that joins it to the rest
senses.definitionCN: 瓶子、弦乐器等物件上细长的连接部分
senses.example: The label was glued around the neck of the bottle.
senses.exampleCN: 标签被粘在瓶颈上。
senses.why: Any object shaped like that bridge lends its narrow joining part the same name, because the picture is a constriction between two wider ends.
senses.whyCN: 任何物件只要长得像那条桥，它的细长连接处就借用了同一个名字，因为画面仍是「两端宽、中间收」。

senses.title: The opening of a garment
senses.definition: the part of a shirt, dress or sweater that surrounds the neck and is shaped to fit it
senses.definitionCN: 衬衫、连衣裙或毛衣上围着脖子、按颈部形状裁出的开口
senses.example: She pulled the sweater down over a wide neck.
senses.exampleCN: 她把毛衣往下拉，盖住宽大的领口。
senses.why: The garment opening sits exactly where the body's neck passes through, so the word transfers from the body to the cloth that surrounds it.
senses.whyCN: 衣服的开口正好位于脖子穿过的地方，于是这个词从身体转到了包住身体的那层布上。

senses.title: A narrow strip of land between waters
senses.definition: a narrow piece of land that joins two larger areas of land and has water on either side
senses.definitionCN: 连接两片较大陆地、两侧临水的狭长地带
senses.example: The village stood on a low neck of land between two bays.
senses.exampleCN: 村子坐落在两个海湾之间一块低矮的地峡上。
senses.why: A strip of land with water on both sides looks like a narrow joining piece, so the same word is used for an isthmus.
senses.whyCN: 两侧临水的一条陆地，看起来就像一块窄窄的连接件，所以同一个词也被用来指地峡。

senses.title: To kiss and hold someone closely, in informal use
senses.definition: in informal speech, to kiss and caress someone while holding them close
senses.definitionCN: 口语中表示搂着某人亲吻、抚摸
senses.example: Two teenagers were necking on a bench by the lake.
senses.exampleCN: 两个少年在湖边的长椅上拥吻。
senses.why: Two people holding each other head to head put their necks close together, and English took the body part as a verb for that embrace.
senses.whyCN: 两个人耳鬓相贴地抱在一起时，脖子挨得最近；英语便拿这个身体部位作动词，指这种拥抱。

intro.en: Neck is a Germanic body word whose deeper origin is uncertain, and it has spread from the body to bottles, clothes and land.
intro.cn: neck 是日耳曼语的身体词，更早的来源不确定；它从身体扩展到瓶子、衣服和土地。

items.en: The deeper origin is uncertain; some accounts link the Germanic word to a root for bending or pressing together, but this is not settled.
items.cn: 更早的来源不确定；有说法把它与表示「弯曲、压紧」的词根联系起来，但并未定论。

items.en: A reconstructed form such as hnakkaz is generally given for the Germanic word for the back of the neck.
items.cn: 一般认为日耳曼语中表示颈背的词有一个类似 hnakkaz 的重构形式。

items.en: Old English hnecca named the neck or nape, and the initial hn- was still pronounced at that stage.
items.cn: 古英语 hnecca 指颈或颈背，当时词首的 hn- 还要发音。

items.en: Middle English dropped the initial h and wrote nekke, the shape that leads towards the modern spelling.
items.cn: 中古英语去掉了词首的 h，写作 nekke，这个形状一路通向现代拼写。

items.en: Modern English keeps neck for the body part and extends it to narrow parts of objects, the opening of clothes, a strip of land and an informal verb.
items.cn: 现代英语保留 neck 指身体部位，并扩展到物件细长处、衣服开口、狭长陆地，还多了一个口语动词。

note.en: The look-alike group collects compounds in which the word survives; the near-meaning group collects neighbouring body and clothing terms.
note.cn: 形近组收仍保留这个词的复合词；近义组收相邻的身体部位与衣着用语。

entries.definition: The line or shape of a garment's opening at the neck.
entries.definitionCN: 衣服领口的线条或形状。

entries.definition: A string of beads or metal worn around the neck.
entries.definitionCN: 戴在脖子上的珠串或金属饰物。

entries.definition: A high collar that covers the neck, or a sweater with one.
entries.definitionCN: 遮住脖子的高领，或带高领的毛衣。

entries.definition: The narrow neck of a bottle, or a point where traffic or work slows down.
entries.definitionCN: 瓶颈；交通或工作中的阻塞点。

entries.definition: The passage inside the neck, used for breathing and swallowing.
entries.definitionCN: 颈部内部用于呼吸和吞咽的通道。

entries.definition: The part of a shirt that stands up around the neck.
entries.definitionCN: 衬衫上围着脖子的那一圈。

entries.definition: The back of the neck.

normalIntro.en: One Old English body word, a lost h, and a habit of naming any narrow join after it: that is the whole history in brief.
normalIntro.cn: 一个古英语身体词、一个消失的 h，以及见到窄连接处就借用的习惯，就是这段历史的大概。

normal.en: Old English hnecca began with hn-, and Middle English simply dropped the h to give nekke.
normal.cn: 古英语 hnecca 以 hn- 开头，中古英语直接把 h 去掉，成了 nekke。

normal.en: Neckline and necklace are compounds that keep the body sense: the line and the jewellery both sit at the neck.
normal.cn: neckline 与 necklace 都是保留身体义的复合词：领口线和首饰都落在脖子处。

normal.en: A bottleneck borrows the shape, not the body: a bottle's narrow part holds traffic or work back.
normal.cn: bottleneck 借的是形状而不是身体：瓶子的细处把交通或工作卡住。

normal.en: Neck and neck pictures two horses whose heads are level, hence the meaning 'exactly equal'.
normal.cn: neck and neck 想像两匹马齐头并进，于是有了「不相上下」的意思。

normal.en: Break one's neck is violent in form but often means rushing dangerously fast.
normal.cn: break one's neck 字面很凶，实际常指拼命赶路、快得危险。

abstract.en: The neck is where a large head is balanced on a narrow support, which is why the word suits any risky narrow join.
abstract.cn: 脖子是让大脑袋架在窄支柱上的地方，所以这个词也适合任何危险的窄连接处。

abstract.en: A garment opening and a body part share one name because cloth is cut to follow the body it covers.
abstract.cn: 衣服开口与身体部位共用一个名字，因为布料是照着它所覆盖的身体裁出来的。

abstract.en: A neck of land is a place where two large worlds touch through a thin corridor.
abstract.cn: 地峡是两片大世界通过一条细走廊相接的地方。

examples.en: The cat rubbed its neck against the door frame.
examples.cn: 猫把脖子蹭在门框上。

examples.en: The label was glued around the neck of the bottle.
examples.cn: 标签被粘在瓶颈上。

examples.en: Two teenagers were necking on a bench by the lake.
examples.cn: 两个少年在湖边的长椅上拥吻。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「奈克」——项链挂在脖子上，英文牌子常印「奈克」；记住 neck 是颈、领口，也是拥吻。

root: 古英语 hnecca（颈；颈背），一般认为源自原始日耳曼语重构形式 hnakkaz，更早的印欧语来源不确定；同族词有 neckline、necklace、turtleneck 等。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a narrow bridge between two wider parts; the senses divide into the body part, narrow parts of objects, a garment opening, a strip of land, and the informal embrace.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是两块宽处之间的窄桥；义项分出身体部位、物件细长处、衣服开口、狭长陆地，以及口语里的拥抱亲吻。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two hands circling the narrow space between a head and a pair of shoulders.
core.cn: 核心意象：一双手环住头部与两肩之间那段窄窄的空间。

branches.en: a scarf wound twice around a child's throat
branches.cn: 围巾在孩子颈上绕了两圈

branches.en: a label glued to the thin part of a bottle
branches.cn: 标签粘在瓶子的细处

branches.en: a sweater cut wide at the opening
branches.cn: 毛衣在领口处裁得很宽

branches.en: two bays joined by a low strip of land
branches.cn: 两个海湾被一条低矮陆地连起

branches.en: two heads leaning together on a bench
branches.cn: 两个脑袋在长椅上靠在一起

intro.en: The entry is built from one Old English noun, an English verb, its endings, and compounds that keep the body sense alive.
intro.cn: 这个词条由一个古英语名词、一个英语动词、它的词尾，以及让身体义延续的复合词搭成。

latinIntro.en: The word is Germanic; Latin cervix, the word for neck, belongs to a different root, so no reliable Latin cognate is listed here.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词属日耳曼语族；拉丁语里表示颈的 cervix 属于另一个词根，所以这里不列可靠的拉丁同族词。

definition_zh: 分（货币单位，一元的百分之一）；分币
definition_en: a coin or unit of money worth one hundredth of the dollar
core_image: 一块钱切成一百小片，每片就是一分
scene: 商店门口的自动门只认硬币，我翻遍口袋又找出一枚最小的硬币。 The doors took every coin but one, and I still owed a single cent.
sceneCN: 这里 cent 是「分」（第 1 个义项：一元的百分之一）；句意是自动门只收硬币，我多找了一分钱。

derivatives.zh: 由 per 加 cent 构成，义为「百分之……；百分比」
由 percent 加 -age 构成，义为「百分率；百分比」
由 cent 加后缀构成，义为「世纪；百年」

senses.title: A coin worth one hundredth of a dollar
senses.definition: a small unit of money; one hundred cents make one dollar
senses.definitionCN: 一百分之一美元的货币单位，一百个分等于一元
senses.example: I paid ninety-nine cents for a bottle of water.
senses.exampleCN: 我花九毛九买了一瓶水。
senses.why: The word names the smallest piece of a dollar, like a slice cut from a whole cake.
senses.whyCN: 这个词指的是一美元最小的一份，像从整块蛋糕上切下的一小片。

senses.title: A very small amount of money
senses.definition: a tiny amount of money, used to show something costs very little or is worthless
senses.definitionCN: 指极少的钱，用来表示某物便宜或不值钱
senses.example: That old comic book is not worth a cent now.
senses.exampleCN: 那本旧连环画现在一文不值。
senses.why: Because a cent is so small, people use it to mean almost nothing at all.
senses.whyCN: 因为分币太小，人们用它表示几乎没有价值。

senses.title: A coin of this value
senses.definition: the actual small coin that represents this unit
senses.definitionCN: 代表这个单位的真实小硬币
senses.example: The machine only takes five and ten cent coins.
senses.exampleCN: 这台机器只收五分和十分硬币。
senses.why: The unit also names the metal coin you can hold in your hand.
senses.whyCN: 这个单位也指能拿在手里的那枚硬币本身。

intro.en: Cent comes straight from Latin, where it meant a hundred.
intro.cn: cent 直接来自拉丁语，本义是「一百」。

items.en: The Latin word centum means a hundred.
items.cn: 拉丁语 centum 意为「一百」。

items.en: French borrowed the idea in words like centime, a small coin.
items.cn: 法语把这个概念用在 centime（一种小硬币）等词里。

items.en: English adopted cent in the fifteenth century mainly in learned words like per cent.
items.cn: 英语在十五世纪吸收 cent，主要用于 per cent 等书面词。

items.en: In 1786 the new United States chose cent as the name of its hundredth coin.
items.cn: 一七八六年，新生的美国选定 cent 作为百分之一硬币的名字。

items.en: Today cent also appears in percent, century and centimetre.
items.cn: 如今 cent 还出现在 percent、century 和 centimetre 里。

note.en: These words all carry the cent root meaning hundred, or sound like cent.
note.cn: 这些词都带有表示「百」的 cent 词根，或与 cent 发音相近。

entries.definition: a period of one hundred years
for every one hundred; out of each hundred
a unit of length equal to one hundredth of a metre
a smell; only the s is extra, the sound is the same
entries.definitionCN: 气味；香气（拼写相近、发音相同，词源不同）

entries.definition: a flat piece of metal used as money
a British coin; before 1971 one hundredth of a pound was a penny
an American coin worth ten cents
an American coin worth five cents

normalIntro.en: Link cent to the family of hundred-words.
normalIntro.cn: 把 cent 和「百」家族的词连起来记。

normal.en: cent = Latin centum, one hundred.
normal.cn: cent 来自拉丁语 centum，意为「一百」。

normal.en: percent = per + cent, out of every hundred.
normal.cn: percent 由 per 加 cent 构成，每百之中。

normal.en: century = cent + -ury, a hundred years.
normal.cn: century 由 cent 构成，一百年。

normal.en: centimetre = centi- + metre, one hundredth of a metre.
normal.cn: centimetre 由 centi- 加 metre 构成，一米百分之一。

normal.en: cent sounds like sent; a letter sent costs money.
normal.cn: cent 发音像 sent；寄一封信要花钱。

abstract.en: Picture one dollar sliced into a hundred tiny pieces.
abstract.cn: 想象一美元被切成一百片小小的碎片。

abstract.en: Picture a single coin rolling along the classroom floor.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚分币在教室地板上滚来滚去。

abstract.en: Picture a piggy bank that smiles when one more cent drops in.
abstract.cn: 想象储蓄罐在又掉进一分钱时开心地笑了。

examples.en: I saved every cent to buy a new schoolbag.
examples.cn: 我省下每一分钱来买一个新书包。

examples.en: The bus fare rose by five cents this month.
examples.cn: 这个月公交车费涨了五分钱。

examples.en: Ninety-nine students came, which is about 90 per cent of the class.
examples.cn: 九十九名学生来了，约占全班的百分之九十。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「森特」——口袋里只有一分钱，森林里的怪兽都嫌少，摇着头说「森特（sent，送）都送不出手」。

root: 拉丁语 centum（一百）。cent 是「百」词根家族的核心，percent（百分之）、century（世纪）、centimetre（厘米）同源。

sensesIntro.en: From a tiny coin to a tiny value.
sensesIntro.cn: 从一枚小硬币引申到极小的价值。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one hundredth of a dollar
core.cn: 核心意象：一美元的百分之一

branches.en: The coin and its unit
branches.cn: 硬币与货币单位

branches.en: A worthless trifle
branches.cn: 不值一文的琐物

branches.en: Money saved coin by coin
branches.cn: 一分一分攒下的钱

branches.en: Cheapness in shopping talk
branches.cn: 购物语境里的便宜

branches.en: Hundredths and smallness
branches.cn: 百分之一与微小

intro.en: Cent is itself a prefix meaning hundred, so its family is easy to spot.
intro.cn: cent 本身就是表示「百」的前缀，它的家族很容易辨认。

latinIntro.en: Latin centum gives these words their hundred meaning.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 centum 赋予这些词「百」的含义。

items.example: A centimetre is one hundredth of a metre.
items.exampleCN: 一厘米是一米的百分之一。

items.example: Eighty per cent of the class passed the test.
items.exampleCN: 全班百分之八十的人通过了考试。

items.meaning: a period of a hundred years
items.example: The school was built a century ago.
items.exampleCN: 这所学校建于一个世纪前。

items.example: The city held a centennial parade.
items.exampleCN: 这座城市举行了百年纪念游行。

items.meaning: an insect with many legs, named for a hundred feet
items.example: A centipede ran across the garden path.
items.exampleCN: 一只蜈蚣跑过花园小径。

items.example: Water boils at one hundred degrees centigrade.
The library celebrated its centenary last year.
items.exampleCN: 图书馆去年庆祝了建馆一百周年。

items.meaning: an officer commanding a hundred Roman soldiers
items.example: The centurion marched at the front of his men.
items.exampleCN: 百夫长走在队伍最前面。

definition_zh: 到达；伸手够到；达到；与…联系；可及范围
definition_en: to arrive at a place; to stretch out a hand to touch something; to attain a level or amount; to get in touch with someone; the distance within which something can be reached
core_image: 手臂伸向高架上的一只杯子
scene: 高架上的杯子有点远，手臂伸到极限才碰到杯沿。 She reached the top shelf with her fingertips.
sceneCN: 这里 reach 是「伸手够到」（第 2 个义项：把手伸出去触到某物）；句意为她用指尖够到了顶层架子。画面里可留意：伸出的手臂、高架上的杯子、碰到的指尖。

pos.zh: 到达；伸手够到；达到；与…联系

derivatives.zh: reach 加 -able，指可到达的、可联系的
out 与 reach 复合，指主动外联、延伸服务
over- 与 reach 复合，指做得过头、超越能力

senses.title: To arrive at a place
senses.definition: to arrive at a place, especially after effort or a journey
senses.definitionCN: 到达某地，尤指经过努力或一段行程之后
senses.example: We reached the village before dark.
senses.exampleCN: 我们在天黑前到达了村子。
senses.why: The oldest sense is to stretch out to a point, and arriving is stretching your journey until it touches the destination.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的意思是「伸到一点」，而抵达就是让行程一直伸到触着目的地。

senses.title: To stretch out and touch
senses.definition: to put out a hand or arm in order to touch or take something
senses.definitionCN: 伸出手或手臂去触到或拿取某物
senses.example: She reached the top shelf with her fingertips.
senses.exampleCN: 她用指尖够到了顶层架子。
senses.why: The word first pictured a hand extended until it met an object, and this literal picture is still the core.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初描绘的是手一直伸到与物体相接，这一字面画面至今仍是核心。

senses.title: To attain a level
senses.definition: to arrive at a particular level, amount or standard after a process
senses.definitionCN: 经过一个过程达到某一水平、数量或标准
senses.example: Sales reached a record high last month.
senses.exampleCN: 上个月的销售额达到了历史新高。
senses.why: If a hand can reach a height, then a process can reach a level, so the word extended from space to measure.
senses.whyCN: 手能伸到一个高度，一个过程也能达到一个水平，于是这个词从空间扩展到度量。

senses.title: To get in touch
senses.definition: to succeed in speaking or writing to someone
senses.definitionCN: 成功地与某人通话或通信
senses.example: I tried to reach him by phone all morning.
senses.exampleCN: 我一上午都在试着打电话联系他。
senses.why: Making contact is like stretching across a distance until the other person is touched, so reach came to mean communicate with.
senses.whyCN: 建立联系就像跨越距离一直伸到触着对方，于是 reach 引申为「与……沟通」。

senses.title: The distance one can reach
senses.definition: the distance or range within which something can be reached or used
senses.definitionCN: 某物能被触及或使用所及的距离或范围
senses.example: The cookies are within the child's reach.
senses.exampleCN: 饼干在孩子够得着的范围内。
senses.why: From the act of stretching came the noun for how far that stretch goes, hence the range one can cover.
senses.whyCN: 从「伸展」的动作生出名词，表示这一伸能到多远，因此就是可覆盖的范围。

intro.en: Reach is a native English word from Old English ræcan, to stretch out or extend, with relatives in other Germanic languages; no Latin source is recorded.
intro.cn: reach 是英语本族词，来自古英语 ræcan（伸出、延伸），在其他日耳曼语言中有亲属词；没有拉丁语来源记录。

items.en: Ræcan meant to stretch out or extend toward something, often a hand toward an object.
items.cn: ræcan 意为向某物伸出或延伸，常指手伸向物体。

items.en: Related Germanic verbs carry the same picture of extending toward a point.
items.cn: 相关的日耳曼语动词带有同样的「朝一点延伸」的画面。

items.en: Middle English reach widened from the hand to the journey, so one could reach a town as well as a shelf.
items.cn: 中古英语 reach 从手扩展到行程，因此既能 reach 一个架子，也能 reach 一座城镇。

items.en: As the word moved from space to levels and to people, it took in reaching a figure and reaching a person.
items.cn: 随着这个词从空间转到水平与人，它纳入了达到某个数字与联系到某个人。

items.en: Modern English uses reach for arriving, stretching, attaining, contacting, and for the range so covered.
items.cn: 现代英语用 reach 表示抵达、伸手、达到、联系，以及由此覆盖的范围。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms and fixed phrases; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of arriving, attaining and contacting.
note.cn: 形近组收派生形式与固定短语；近义组收表示抵达、达到与联系的动词。

entries.definition: Able to be reached.
To extend a hand or make contact.
To stretch a hand toward something.
To go too far or attempt too much.
To get to a place.
To reach a level or goal after effort.
entries.definitionCN: 经过努力达到某一水平或目标。

entries.definition: To extend a limb or a thing.
To get in touch with someone.

normalIntro.en: The word starts with a hand stretched out, then covers journeys, levels, people and the range so covered.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词从伸出的手开始，随后涵盖行程、水平、人，以及由此覆盖的范围。

normal.en: Reach and stretch share the picture of something extended toward a point.
normal.cn: reach 与 stretch 共享「某物朝一点伸展」的画面。

normal.en: You reach a shelf with a hand and reach a city with a journey.
normal.cn: 用手 reach 一个架子，用一段行程 reach 一座城市。

normal.en: Prices reaching a record high is the same word used for a level.
normal.cn: 价格 reaching a record high，是同一个词用在水平上。

normal.en: To reach someone is to stretch across the distance until contact is made.
normal.cn: to reach 某人，就是跨越距离一直伸到建立联系。

normal.en: Within reach means close enough to touch or use.
normal.cn: within reach 意为近得足以触及或使用。

abstract.en: Reach measures the distance between effort and its object.
abstract.cn: reach 衡量的是努力与其目标之间的距离。

abstract.en: What is out of reach is not always out of mind.
abstract.cn: 够不着的东西，并不总是不在心上的。

abstract.en: To reach out is to shorten a distance that other people cannot shorten alone.
abstract.cn: reach out 就是缩短一段别人无法独自缩短的距离。

examples.en: We reached the village before dark.
examples.cn: 我们在天黑前到达了村子。

examples.en: She reached the top shelf with her fingertips.
examples.cn: 她用指尖够到了顶层架子。

examples.en: I tried to reach him by phone all morning.
examples.cn: 我一上午都在试着打电话联系他。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「瑞奇」——手臂一直伸出去，够到架子上的杯子，记住 reach 是到达、够到。

sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「朝一点伸展」；义项分为抵达、触到、达到、联系，以及由此覆盖的范围。

definition_zh: 普通的；常见的；共同的
definition_en: happening often, shared by many people, or ordinary and not special
core_image: 大家都有的、随处可见的
scene: 小区门口天天有人遛狗，几只金毛总能碰上。 Pandas are rare but sparrows are common birds.
sceneCN: 这里 common 是「常见的」（第 1 个义项：经常出现、数量多）；句意是熊猫稀有而麻雀常见。

senses.title: Seen or happening often
senses.definition: found or happening often and in many places
senses.definitionCN: 经常出现、到处都有的
senses.example: Colds are common in winter.
senses.exampleCN: 冬天感冒很常见。
senses.why: What belongs to many must show up everywhere, so the everyday look became the first sense.
senses.whyCN: 属于众人的东西自然到处出现，「常见」便成了第一义。

senses.title: Shared by two or more people
senses.definition: belonged to or shared by two or more people or groups
senses.definitionCN: 由两个或以上的人、群体共同拥有的
senses.example: Li Lei and I have English songs in common.
senses.exampleCN: 李雷和我都爱英文歌。
senses.why: The same root that means together also means shared.
senses.whyCN: 词根既有「一起」的意思，也就有了「共享」之义。

senses.title: Ordinary and not special
senses.definition: not special or unusual in any way
senses.definitionCN: 毫无特别之处的
senses.example: He is just a common student like us.
senses.exampleCN: 他只是个像我们一样的普通学生。
senses.why: What everyone has feels ordinary to each one.
senses.whyCN: 人人都有之物，在个人眼里便显得平凡。

senses.title: Belonging to the people as a whole
senses.definition: belonging to everyone in a community, as in common land
senses.definitionCN: 属于全体社区成员的，如公地
senses.example: Villagers let their sheep eat on the common grass.
senses.exampleCN: 村民让羊群在公地上吃草。
senses.why: Shared things widen to things shared by a whole village.
senses.whyCN: 「共享」的范围扩大到全村共有之物。

intro.en: Common comes from Latin words for sharing together.
intro.cn: common 来自拉丁语「共同分享」的词根。

items.en: Latin communis meant shared by all, public, from com- together and munis bound to serve.
items.cn: 拉丁语 communis 意为人人所共有的，来自 com-（一起）与 munis（尽义务的）。

items.en: Latin communia named things held in common.
items.cn: 拉丁语 communia 指共有之物。

items.en: Old French comun passed the word to England.
items.cn: 古法语 comun 把这个词传入英格兰。

items.en: Middle English commun covered shared, ordinary and public senses.
items.cn: 中古英语 commun 涵盖共有、普通、公共三层意思。

items.en: Modern English common built phrases like common sense and in common.
items.cn: 现代英语 common 衍生出 common sense、in common 等短语。

note.en: The first group collects the same-root family; the second collects words close in meaning.
note.cn: 第一组收同根词，第二组收近义词。

entries.definition: Happening as always.
Used or had together.

normalIntro.en: Remember common through sharing and everyday life.
normalIntro.cn: 从「共享」与日常生活记 common。

normal.en: common sense means good everyday judgement.
normal.cn: common sense 指生活常识与判断力。

normal.en: The commons is land for everyone.

abstract.cn: 想象大家围着一张大桌子吃饭。

abstract.en: See the same grey jacket on many people.

abstract.en: Hear a song everyone in class can sing.
abstract.cn: 听一首全班都会唱的歌。

examples.en: Misreading in haste is a common mistake in exams.
examples.cn: 匆忙中看错题是考试里常见的错误。

examples.en: Our class found many interests in common during the talk.
examples.cn: 聊天时我们班发现彼此有许多共同爱好。

examples.en: Riding a bike to school is common among students here.
examples.cn: 在这里，骑自行车上学在学生中很普遍。

sensesIntro.cn: common 从常见之物走向共同爱好与公共用地。

definition_en: to put something down flat or in position, to produce eggs, and to prepare or present something such as a table or a claim
core_image: 一双手把一块布平平地铺在桌面上，四角一一压好
scene: 晚饭前，厨房里碗碟碰得轻响。 She laid the table before the guests arrived.

senses.title: To put something down flat or in place
senses.definition: to place something down carefully, especially so that it lies flat on a surface
senses.definitionCN: 小心地把某物放下，尤指使其平贴在表面上
senses.example: He laid the map flat on the desk.
senses.exampleCN: 他把地图平铺在书桌上。
senses.why: The Old English verb was the causative partner of to lie: it meant to make something lie down, which is exactly the picture of placing an object flat.
senses.whyCN: 这个古英语动词是「躺」的使役对应词，意为「使某物躺下」，正是一幅把东西平放下去的画面。

senses.title: To produce eggs
senses.definition: to produce an egg from the body, used of birds, fish, reptiles and insects
senses.definitionCN: 从体内产出卵，用于鸟、鱼、爬行动物和昆虫
senses.example: The hen lays an egg almost every morning.
senses.exampleCN: 这只母鸡几乎每天早上下一枚蛋。
senses.why: An egg is deposited on a surface the way an object is laid down, so the same verb covers both the careful placing and the dropping of an egg.
senses.whyCN: 蛋被安置在某个表面上，就像物件被放下，于是同一个动词既指小心摆放，也指把蛋产下。

senses.title: To prepare and set a table
senses.definition: to arrange plates, knives and other items in their places for a meal
senses.definitionCN: 把盘碟、刀叉等按位置摆好，准备用餐
senses.example: She laid the table before the guests arrived.
senses.exampleCN: 客人到来之前她把餐桌摆好了。
senses.why: Setting a table is a series of small placements, each item laid in its own place, so the general sense of placing turns into the household ritual.
senses.whyCN: 摆餐桌是一连串小小的放置动作，每件东西都被放在自己的位置上，于是泛泛的「放置」义变成了家庭里的固定仪式。

senses.title: To present or put forward a claim
senses.definition: to put forward a claim, a charge or a responsibility for others to consider
senses.definitionCN: 提出主张、指控或责任，供他人考虑
senses.example: The workers laid their demands before the manager.
senses.exampleCN: 工人们把他们的要求摆到了经理面前。
senses.why: A claim is placed before someone as a document is placed on a table, so the physical act of laying supplies the metaphor for formal demands.
senses.whyCN: 主张被摆到某人面前，就像文件被放到桌上，于是「放置」这一物理动作提供了正式诉求的比喻。

intro.en: Lay is the Old English causative of lie: to lay something is to make it lie, and the two verbs have been confusing writers ever since.
intro.cn: lay 是古英语中 lie 的使役形式：把某物 lay 就是使它 lie，这两个动词从此一直让写作者犯难。

items.en: Lecgan meant to cause something to lie down, the causative partner of licgan, to lie.
items.cn: lecgan 意为使某物躺下，是 licgan（躺）的使役对应词。

items.en: Licgan was the intransitive verb to lie; the pair survives as lay and lie, which still confuse writers.
items.cn: licgan 是不及物动词「躺」；这一对至今保存为 lay 与 lie，仍让写作者混淆。

items.en: Middle English leyen kept the idea of placing something down, and the past tense ledde later became laid.
items.cn: 中古英语 leyen 保留「把东西放下」的意思，过去式 ledde 后来变为 laid。

items.en: Lay widened into set phrases such as lay the table, lay a trap and lay a claim, all built on placing something in position.
items.cn: lay 扩展到 lay the table、lay a trap、lay a claim 等固定说法，都建立在「把东西放到位」。

items.en: Modern English keeps laid as the past of lay, and the egg sense survives in farming and everyday speech.
items.cn: 现代英语保留 laid 为 lay 的过去式，产卵义在农业与日常口语中都还在用。

note.en: The look-alike group collects forms and derivatives of lay; the near-meaning group collects verbs for placing, including the pair that is most often confused with it.
note.cn: 形近组收 lay 的各种形式与派生词；近义组收表示放置的动词，包括最常与它混淆的那个词。

entries.definitionCN: 覆盖在另一层之上的一层材料。

entries.definition: To put something in a particular position.
To move something into a position, the most general verb of placing.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物移到某个位置，最泛用的放置动词。

entries.definition: To put something in place carefully, often for a purpose.
entries.definitionCN: 为某个目的小心地把某物放好。

entries.definition: To rest flat on a surface, the intransitive partner of lay.
entries.definitionCN: 平躺在表面上，是 lay 的不及物对应词。

normalIntro.en: The word is the active partner of lie, and its short forms hide an irregular past that catches almost every learner.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是 lie 的主动对应词，它简短的形式里藏着一个几乎能难住每个学习者的不规则过去式。

normal.en: Lay is to lie as raise is to rise: lay needs an object, because something else is being made to lie.
normal.cn: lay 与 lie 的关系就像 raise 与 rise：lay 需要宾语，因为是别的东西被弄得躺下。

normal.en: The past tense is laid, never layed, which is the spelling mistake to watch for.
normal.cn: 过去式是 laid，绝不是 layed，这是最要提防的拼写错误。

normal.en: Lay the table is a fixed phrase, so the placing sense became a household routine.
normal.cn: lay the table 是固定说法，于是「放置」义成了家庭日常。

normal.en: A hen lays an egg because the egg is deposited, which is the same downward placement.
normal.cn: 母鸡 lay an egg，因为蛋被安置下来，仍是同一种向下的放置。

normal.en: Layout and layer both build on lay: an arrangement and a thickness placed over something.
normal.cn: layout 与 layer 都由 lay 构成：一个是排布，一个是铺在上面的厚度。

abstract.en: One verb covers plates, eggs and claims because all three are put down where someone will find them.
abstract.cn: 一个动词涵盖盘子、蛋和主张，因为三者都被放在别人能找到的地方。

abstract.en: The difference between lay and lie is the difference between doing something to a thing and doing something to yourself.
abstract.cn: lay 与 lie 的差别，就是对别的东西做一件事，还是对自己做一件事。

abstract.en: Every table laid before a meal is a small act of arranging the future.
abstract.cn: 每张餐前摆好的桌子，都是一次安排未来的小小动作。

definition_zh: 适当的；正确的；合乎礼节的；专有的；特有的；本身的
definition_en: suitable and correct for a situation, belonging to one thing alone, or, in grammar, naming a particular person or place
core_image: 一件东西落进专为它留出的那个位置，不偏不倚，正正好好
scene: 正式晚宴前，主人把刀叉一件件摆正，餐巾折好放在盘子左侧。 She checked that every guest had the proper glass beside the plate.
sceneCN: 这里取「适当的、合乎场合的」意思（第 1 个义项：适合当时场合与规矩的）；句意为她逐一确认每位客人的盘边都放着该配的那只酒杯。摆正刀叉的动作就是线索。

pos.zh: 适当的；正确的；合乎礼节的；专有的；特有的；本身的

derivatives.zh: 由 proper 加 -ly 构成，义为「适当地；正确地」
由拉丁 proprietas 经法语进入英语，义为「财产；性质」
与 proper 同出拉丁 proprietas，义为「得体；礼节」
在拉丁词干 propri- 前加 ad-，义为「合适的」

senses.title: Suitable and correct for the situation
senses.definition: right or suitable for a particular situation, purpose or person
senses.definitionCN: 对某种场合、用途或某人来说正确或合适的
senses.example: Use the proper tool for the job.
senses.exampleCN: 干这活要用合适的工具。
senses.why: Latin proprius meant one's own, and what belongs to a thing is exactly what fits it, so the sense slid from belonging to being the right one.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 proprius 意为「自己的」，而属于某物的东西恰恰就是适合它的东西，于是词义从「属于」滑到「正是该用的那一个」。

senses.title: Belonging to one thing alone
senses.definition: belonging by nature to one particular thing, person or group and not to any other
senses.definitionCN: 天然属于某一特定事物、人或群体，而不属于其他
senses.example: This bird is proper to the island and lives nowhere else.
senses.exampleCN: 这种鸟是该岛特有的，别处见不到。
senses.why: The root sense of own is plainest here: a quality proper to something is a quality that belongs to it and to nothing else, which is why the word so often appears with to.
senses.whyCN: 「自己的」这层本义在这里最清楚：proper to 某物的性质，就是只属于它、不属于别处的性质，所以这个词常与 to 连用。

senses.title: Strictly so called
senses.definition: used after a noun to mean the central part of a place or thing, as opposed to the area around it
senses.definitionCN: 用在名词后，指某地或某物的中心部分，以区别于其外围
senses.example: The market lies outside the old town proper.
senses.exampleCN: 市场位于老城区本身之外。
senses.why: If something is its own, the word can mark the thing itself as against its outskirts, and that is exactly how the after-noun use arose.
senses.whyCN: 既然某物是「它自己的」，这个词就能标出「事物本身」以区别于外围；后置用法正是这样长出来的。

senses.title: Naming one particular individual
senses.definition: in grammar, naming a particular person, place or thing rather than a whole class of them
senses.definitionCN: 语法上指称某个特定的人、地或物，而不是一整类
senses.example: Paris is a proper noun and city is a common noun.
senses.exampleCN: Paris 是专有名词，city 是普通名词。
senses.why: A proper noun belongs to a single bearer instead of a whole class, so the grammatical term preserves the old idea of exclusive ownership.
senses.whyCN: 专有名词只属于一个承担者而不属于一整类，所以这个语法术语保留的仍是「排他地拥有」这层旧义。

senses.title: Socially correct and respectable
senses.definition: behaving in the way polite society considers correct and respectable
senses.definitionCN: 按照讲究礼数的社会所认可、体面的方式行事
senses.example: It is not proper to ask about someone's salary.
senses.exampleCN: 打听别人的薪水不合规矩。
senses.why: A community decides what belongs to a well-run occasion, so propriety became a matter of manners and the adjective took on the sense of socially correct.
senses.whyCN: 一个共同体认定什么才属于「办得体面的场合」，于是 proper 也成了举止问题，形容词便带上「合乎社交规矩」的意思。

intro.en: Proper goes back to a Latin adjective meaning one's own, and every later sense is a variation on belonging.
intro.cn: proper 上溯到一个意为「自己的」的拉丁形容词，后来所有义项都是「归属」这一点的变奏。

items.en: Proprius meant one's own, personal, not shared with others; a common but uncertain explanation derives it from pro privo, for a private person.
items.cn: proprius 意为自己的、个人的、不与他人共有的；一般认为它与 pro privo（为了私人）有关，但这一解释并不确定。

items.en: The noun proprietas named ownership and also the quality that belongs to a thing and makes it what it is.
items.cn: 名词 proprietas 指所有权，也指属于某物、使该物成为其自身的性质。

items.en: Old French propre kept the senses of one's own, suitable and also clean or neat.
items.cn: 古法语 propre 保留了「自己的」「合适的」，以及「干净整洁的」这几层意思。

items.en: Middle English proper first meant belonging to someone or something, and older texts also use it for fine or excellent.
items.cn: 中古英语的 proper 最初指「属于某人或某物的」，较早的文本里还用它表示「出色的、优良的」。

items.en: Modern English settles on suitable, exclusive and strict, and keeps the old ownership in property, propriety, appropriate and the grammatical proper noun.
items.cn: 现代英语把词义定为「合适的、专属的、严格意义上的」，并把「归属」的旧义留在 property、propriety、appropriate 以及语法术语 proper noun 里。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the Latin adjective for one's own; the near-meaning group gathers words about fitting and good manners.
note.cn: 形近组收同一拉丁「自己的」形容词上的词；近义组收关于「合适」与「礼节」的词。

entries.definition: Something owned, or a quality belonging to a thing.
entries.definitionCN: 拥有的东西，或某物具有的性质。

entries.definition: Correctness of behaviour, good manners.
Suitable for a particular purpose or occasion.
The owner of a business or a property.
Right for a purpose or a person.
Appropriate to the occasion.
Polite and correct in behaviour.
Considered decent and proper by others.
entries.definitionCN: 被他人视为正派得体的。

normalIntro.en: The word starts from ownership and ends in fitness, and the whole family still turns on the question of what belongs where.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词从「归属」出发，走到「合宜」，整族词始终围绕「什么该在什么位置」这一问题。

normal.en: Latin proprius means one's own, so proper is about ownership before it is ever about manners.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 proprius 意为「自己的」，所以 proper 先说归属，之后才说礼节。

normal.en: Property and propriety share the same stem: what one owns, and what it is fitting to own or to do.
normal.cn: property 与 propriety 同一词干：一个是拥有的东西，一个是拥有或行事是否得体。

normal.en: The grammatical proper noun keeps the old sense, since such a name is owned by one person or one place.
normal.cn: 语法术语 proper noun 保留了旧义，因为这类名字只被一个人或一个地方拥有。

normal.en: After a noun, as in the city proper, the word marks the thing itself rather than the area around it.
normal.cn: 放在名词后，如 the city proper，这个词标出的是事物本身，而不是它周边的地带。

normal.en: Appropriate adds ad-, to, to the same stem: to make something one's own, and therefore to make it fit.
normal.cn: appropriate 在同一词干前加 ad-（向），意为「使成为自己的」，因此也就是「使之合宜」。

abstract.en: What is proper to a thing is what cannot be taken from it without changing what it is.
abstract.cn: 某物所专属的东西，一旦被拿走，它就不再是原来的它。

abstract.en: Manners and grammar seem far apart, yet both use proper to decide what belongs where.
abstract.cn: 礼节与语法看似相隔很远，却都用 proper 来判定什么该在什么位置。

abstract.en: A word for ownership became a word for correctness because fitting in has always been a matter of belonging.
abstract.cn: 一个表示「拥有」的词变成了表示「正确」的词，因为「合宜」从来就是「归属」的另一面。

examples.en: Use the proper tool for the job.
examples.cn: 干这活要用合适的工具。

examples.en: Paris is a proper noun and city is a common noun.
examples.cn: Paris 是专有名词，city 是普通名词。

examples.en: The market lies outside the old town proper.
examples.cn: 市场位于老城区本身之外。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「普若破」——听着像「铺得正」，铺得正正好好，就是适当。

root: 拉丁语 proprius（自己的、专属的），深层来源一般认为与「私人、个别」有关，但具体构成存疑；经古法语 propre 进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: The core is belonging, and the senses fan out from it: what fits because it belongs, what belongs to one thing only, the thing itself, a name owned by one bearer, and the manners a community expects.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「归属」，义项由它散开：因为属于所以合宜、只属于一物的特性、事物本身、只被一个对象拥有的名字，以及共同体期待的礼节。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an object dropping neatly into the one slot cut for it, with no gap on any side.
core.cn: 核心意象：一件东西落进专为它挖出的那个凹槽，四边不留缝隙。

branches.en: a tool that fits the hand exactly
branches.cn: 正好合手的一把工具

branches.en: a bird found on one island only
branches.cn: 只在一座岛上出现的鸟

branches.en: a map where the old town sits inside its ring road
branches.cn: 旧城被环路围住的城区图

branches.en: a capital letter at the start of a name
branches.cn: 名字开头的那个大写字母

branches.en: a guest choosing the right fork
branches.cn: 客人挑对那把叉子

intro.en: A Latin adjective of ownership and the noun built from it hold the word together, and English suffixes turn the same stem into adverbs, nouns and related adjectives.
intro.cn: 表示归属的拉丁语形容词及由其构成的名词共同支撑这个词，英语后缀又把同一词干变成副词、名词和相关形容词。

latinIntro.en: Latin proprius, one's own, and the noun proprietas, ownership or peculiar quality, are the direct sources of the English word and of its relatives.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语形容词 proprius（自己的）与名词 proprietas（所有权、特性）是英语这个词及其同族词的直接来源。

items.meaning: ownership, a quality of one's own

definition_zh: 呼吸；呼出；低声说；注入（活力）
definition_en: to take air into the lungs and let it out, to send air or words out softly, or to fill something with life or a quality
core_image: 胸腔一起一伏，把空气吸进来再送出去
scene: 潜水员浮出水面，摘下呼吸管，深深地吸了一口空气。 The diver surfaced, took off the tube and began to breathe deeply.
sceneCN: 这里 breathe 是「呼吸」（第 1 个义项：把空气吸入肺里再呼出）；句意为潜水员浮出水面，摘下管子，开始深呼吸。

pos.zh: 动词：呼吸；呼出；低声说；注入

derivatives.zh: 与 breathe 同源，义为「呼吸；一口气」
由 breathe 加 -ing 构成，义为「呼吸；呼吸动作」
由 breathe 加 -able 构成，义为「可以呼吸的；透气的」
由 breathe 加 -er 构成，义为「短暂的休息；喘口气」

senses.title: To take air in and out
senses.definition: to take air into the lungs and let it out again
senses.definitionCN: 把空气吸入肺里再呼出来
senses.example: Fish cannot breathe out of water.
senses.exampleCN: 鱼离开水就无法呼吸。
senses.why: The verb grew beside the noun breath, naming the act of moving air in and out of the body.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词在名词 breath 旁边发展出来，用来指把空气送进身体再送出去的动作。

senses.title: To send out air or soft words
senses.definition: to send air out of the body, or to say something in a soft voice
senses.definitionCN: 把空气送出体外，或以轻柔的声音说话
senses.example: She breathed a quiet warning in his ear.
senses.exampleCN: 她在他耳边低声警告了一句。
senses.why: The air that leaves the mouth can carry a whisper, so the same act came to mean speaking softly.
senses.whyCN: 离开嘴边的空气可以承载耳语，于是同一个动作又用来指轻声说话。

senses.title: To fill with life or a quality
senses.definition: to give life, energy or a particular quality to something
senses.definitionCN: 给某物注入生命、活力或某种特质
senses.example: The new players breathed life into the team.
senses.exampleCN: 新队员给球队注入了活力。
senses.why: Breath is the visible sign of life, so pouring breath into a thing means waking it up.
senses.whyCN: 呼吸是生命可见的标志，所以把气息灌进某物，就意味着让它活起来。

intro.en: Breathe is the old verb formed from breath, and it has kept the sense of moving air ever since.
intro.cn: breathe 是由 breath 构成的古老动词，一直保留着「让空气流动」的意思。

items.en: Braethian was the verb built on braeth, meaning to send out vapour or air.
items.cn: braethian 是建立在 braeth 之上的动词，意为呼出蒸气或空气。

items.en: German brodeln and Dutch braemen keep the sense of steaming or breathing out.
items.cn: 德语 brodeln 与荷兰语 braemen 保留了「冒气、呼出」的意思。

items.en: The verb settled as breathe and took the full sense of taking air in and out.
items.cn: 这个动词固定为 breathe，并获得了「吸入与呼出空气」的完整含义。

items.en: Because a whisper rides on the breath, the verb also came to mean to say something softly.
items.cn: 因为耳语随气息而出，这个动词也引申为轻声说话。

items.en: Today breathe covers breathing, whispering and giving life to something.
items.cn: 今天 breathe 覆盖呼吸、低声细语，以及给某物注入生命。

note.en: The first group collects words close in shape or sound; the second group collects words about air and life.
note.cn: 第一组收拼写或读音接近的词，第二组收与空气、生命有关的词。

entries.definition: The noun for one amount of air taken in.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「呼吸；一口气」，与 breathe 同源。

entries.definition: A light, pleasant wind.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「微风」，读音与 breathe 接近。

entries.definition: To twist flowers or cloth into a ring.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「编成花环；缠绕」，拼写与 breathe 相近。

entries.definition: To draw air into the lungs.
To send air out of the lungs.
To speak in a very quiet voice.

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the recorded history, the real family and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用有记录的历史、真实词族和这个词实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: Breathe is the old verb made from the noun breath, and the pair still work together.
normal.cn: breathe 是由名词 breath 构成的古老动词，这一对至今配合使用。

normal.en: The air that leaves the mouth can carry a whisper, which is why the verb also means to speak softly.
normal.cn: 离开嘴边的空气能承载耳语，所以这个动词也指轻声说话。

normal.en: Breath is the visible sign of life, so breathing life into something wakes it up.
normal.cn: 呼吸是生命可见的标志，所以给某物 breathe life 就是让它活起来。

normal.en: It often pairs with deeply, in, out and life.
normal.cn: 它常与 deeply、in、out、life 搭配。

normal.en: Spell b-r-e-a-t-h-e; the final e marks the verb, and the ea sounds long.
normal.cn: 拼写是 b-r-e-a-t-h-e，词尾 e 标记动词，ea 读长音。

abstract.en: See a chest rise and fall like a slow wave: that motion is to breathe.
abstract.cn: 想象胸腔像慢波一样一起一伏：这个动作就是 breathe。

abstract.en: Let that outgoing wave carry a whisper, and the same picture turns into soft speech.
abstract.cn: 让呼出的那道波带走一句耳语，同一幅画面就变成轻声说话。

abstract.en: Say the word aloud, then let the rising chest bring the meaning back.
abstract.cn: 先把这个词读出声，再让起伏的胸腔把意思带回来。

examples.en: Fish cannot breathe out of water.
examples.cn: 鱼离开水就无法呼吸。

examples.en: She breathed a quiet warning in his ear.
examples.cn: 她在他耳边低声警告了一句。

examples.en: The new players breathed life into the team.
examples.cn: 新队员给球队注入了活力。

root: breathe 是建立在名词 breath 之上的古英语动词 braethian，原意为呼出蒸气或空气，与德语 brodeln、荷兰语 braemen 有相近含义。它后来获得「吸入与呼出空气」的完整意义；因为耳语随气息而出，又引申为轻声说话；因为呼吸是生命可见的标志，再引申为给某物注入生命或活力。

sensesIntro.en: All three senses of breathe rest on one picture: air moving in and out of the body.
sensesIntro.cn: breathe 的三个义项都立在同一个画面上：空气进出身体。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a chest rising and falling as air moves in and out
core.cn: 核心意象：胸腔一起一伏，空气进出

branches.en: THE AIR: moving air in and out is the first and literal sense.
branches.cn: 空气线：空气进出是第一个也是最字面的义项。

branches.en: THE WHISPER: outgoing air can carry soft words.
branches.cn: 耳语线：呼出的气可以承载轻柔的话语。

branches.en: THE LIFE: breath poured into a thing wakes it up.
branches.cn: 生命线：把气息灌进某物，就让它活起来。

branches.en: THE OUTGOING: breathing out and whispering share one stream of air.
branches.cn: 呼出线：呼气与耳语共享同一股气流。

branches.en: THE SPIRIT: a whisper and a life-giving breath both move unseen air.
branches.cn: 气息线：耳语与赋予生命的气息都在推动看不见的空气。

intro.en: Breathe is a base verb, so the items below are its endings and the words it joins.
intro.cn: breathe 是基础动词，下面列出的是它的词尾以及与之组合的词。

latinIntro.en: Latin spirare means to breathe; it is a parallel verb, not the source of breathe.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 spirare 意为「呼吸」，它是平行词，不是 breathe 的来源。

items.example: Braethian is the recorded Old English source.
items.exampleCN: braethian 是有记录的古英语来源。

definition_zh: 科学的；科学研究的；严谨系统的
definition_en: relating to science or its methods, or careful and systematic in approach
core_image: 研究者戴着护目镜，把样本放进仪器，旁边的记录表写得整整齐齐
scene: 研究团队用科学的方法检验这个说法。 The team used a scientific method to test the claim.
sceneCN: 这里 scientific 是「科学的」（第 1 个义项）；句意：研究团队用科学的方法检验这个说法。

derivatives.zh: 科学
科学家
科学地
不科学的

senses.title: Relating to science
senses.definition: connected with science or the work of scientists
senses.definitionCN: 与科学或科学家的工作有关的
senses.example: They need scientific evidence.
senses.exampleCN: 他们需要科学证据。
senses.why: The main sense points to the field of science.
senses.whyCN: 主要义项指向科学领域。

senses.title: Careful and systematic
senses.definition: done in a careful, organized, and testable way
senses.definitionCN: 以谨慎、有条理且可检验的方式进行的
senses.example: Her approach is scientific and careful.
senses.exampleCN: 她的方法严谨而细致。
senses.why: The method of science becomes a general style of thinking.
senses.whyCN: 科学方法变成一种普遍的思维方式。

senses.title: Used in science
senses.definition: designed or used for scientific work
senses.definitionCN: 为科学工作设计或使用的
senses.example: The lab bought scientific instruments.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室购买了科学仪器。
senses.why: Objects and tools take the label of the field they serve.
senses.whyCN: 物品与工具以所服务领域的名称来命名。

intro.en: Scientific combines Latin scientia, knowledge, with the ending fic, making.
intro.cn: scientific 由拉丁语 scientia（知识）与表示「造成」的结尾 fic 组合而成。

items.en: Scientia meant knowledge.
items.cn: scientia 意为知识。

items.en: Scientificus meant producing knowledge.
items.cn: scientificus 意为产生知识的。

items.en: Scientific entered English meaning producing knowledge.
items.cn: scientific 进入英语时意为产生知识的。

items.en: It came to mean relating to science.
items.cn: 它开始表示与科学有关的。

items.en: Scientific also means systematic and careful.
items.cn: 现代英语中 scientific 还表示系统严谨的。

note.en: Scientific is compared with related forms and with adjectives for careful inquiry.
note.cn: 把 scientific 与相关词形以及表示严谨探究的形容词作比较。

entries.definition: a person who studies science
in a scientific way
systematic knowledge
done according to a clear plan
based on observation or experiment
very careful and exact

normalIntro.en: Scientific is the adjective of science, formed with the ending fic.
normalIntro.cn: scientific 是 science 的形容词，由结尾 fic 构成。

normal.en: Scientific method is a careful way to test ideas.
normal.cn: 科学方法是检验想法的严谨方式。

normal.en: Scientific evidence supports a claim.
normal.cn: 科学证据支持某个说法。

normal.en: The scientific community shares results.
normal.cn: 科学界共享研究结果。

normal.en: Unscientific means not based on science.
normal.cn: unscientific 意为不科学的。

normal.en: Scientific and science share the sci base.
normal.cn: scientific 与 science 共享 sci 词干。

abstract.en: The ending fic means making, so scientific once meant knowledge-making.
abstract.cn: 结尾 fic 意为造成，因此 scientific 原意为「产生知识的」。

abstract.en: Science as a method becomes an adjective for any careful work.
abstract.cn: 科学作为一种方法，其形容词可形容任何严谨工作。

abstract.en: To call work scientific is to demand evidence.
abstract.cn: 称一项工作为科学的，就是要求证据。

examples.en: They need scientific evidence.

examples.cn: 这个说法没有科学依据。

examples.en: The lab bought scientific instruments.
examples.cn: 实验室购买了科学仪器。

root: 由 science（科学）加后缀 fic（产生……的）构成，远源为拉丁语 scientia（知识）与 facere（做）。

sensesIntro.en: Scientific means relating to science, careful and systematic, or used for scientific work.
sensesIntro.cn: scientific 意为与科学有关的、严谨系统的，或用于科学工作的。

core.en: Marked by the methods and standards of science.
core.cn: 具有科学方法与标准的。

branches.en: Connected with the field of science.
branches.cn: 与科学领域相关。

branches.en: Done with care, order, and tests.
branches.cn: 以谨慎、条理与检验完成。

branches.en: Tools made for research work.
branches.cn: 为研究工作制造的器具。

branches.en: The field and its method reinforce each other.
branches.cn: 领域与方法相互强化。

branches.en: Instruments serve careful inquiry.
branches.cn: 仪器服务于严谨探究。

intro.en: Scientific joins the science family of knowledge words.
intro.cn: scientific 加入由知识词汇构成的 science 词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin scientificus is the direct model.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 scientificus 是直接构词模型。

items.meaning: the group of scientists as a whole

definition_zh: 便士；一便士硬币；美分；（否定）一分钱
definition_en: a small British coin worth one hundredth of a pound, its value as a unit of money, or an American one-cent coin
core_image: 一枚磨得发亮的铜色小圆片躺在掌心
scene: 集市收摊时，摊主把零散的硬币一枚枚数进铁盒。 She counted the pennies into a small tin box.
sceneCN: 这里是「一便士硬币」（第 2 个义项：一枚枚具体的硬币）；句意为她把一便士硬币数进小铁盒。

pos.zh: 便士；一便士硬币；美分；一分钱

collocations.zh: 你在想什么呢（想听听你的想法）

collocations.phrase: in for a penny, in for a pound

derivatives.zh: 由 penny 加表示「没有」的后缀 -less 构成，义为「身无分文的」
由 penny 与 worth 复合而成，义为「一便士的货量；少量」
由 six 与 pence 复合而成，指英国旧时的六便士硬币
由 penny 与 pinching 复合而成，义为「吝啬的」

senses.title: A unit of British money
senses.definition: a unit of money in Britain, worth one hundredth of a pound, used mainly when stating prices and amounts
senses.definitionCN: 英国的货币单位，等于一英镑的百分之一，主要用于说明价格和金额
senses.example: The stamp costs fifty pence.
senses.exampleCN: 这张邮票要五十便士。
senses.why: When the coin is treated as a value on a price tag, English uses pence, the old plural that behaves like a unit rather than a set of objects.
senses.whyCN: 当这枚钱被当成价签上的数值时，英语用 pence；这个旧复数更像一个计量单位，而不是一堆具体物件。

senses.title: A single British coin
senses.definition: the small coin itself, especially when you count or hold separate pieces
senses.definitionCN: 指那枚小硬币本身，尤指数着一枚枚、拿在手里的零散硬币
senses.example: He dropped two pennies into the jar.
senses.exampleCN: 他把两枚一便士硬币投进罐子。
senses.why: The regular plural pennies is kept for the physical pieces, so English can tell the object in your palm from the figure on a receipt.
senses.whyCN: 规则复数 pennies 留给一枚枚实物，因此英语能区分手心那枚东西和收据上的那个数字。

senses.title: An American one-cent coin
senses.definition: in American informal use, a coin worth one cent, or one cent itself
senses.definitionCN: 在美式口语中，指值一分的硬币，或指一分钱
senses.example: The machine only takes pennies and nickels.
senses.exampleCN: 这台机器只收一分和五分硬币。
senses.why: American speech kept the old Germanic name for small change instead of the Latin cent, so penny crossed the Atlantic with a new value.
senses.whyCN: 美国口语保留了表示零钱的古老日耳曼名称，而没有用拉丁来源的 cent，于是 penny 漂过大西洋后换了面值。

senses.title: The smallest amount of money
senses.definition: used after a negative to mean no money at all, or an amount too small to matter
senses.definitionCN: 用在否定词之后，表示一分钱也没有，或指少到无关紧要的钱
senses.example: It did not cost me a penny.
senses.exampleCN: 这没花我一分钱。
senses.why: Since a penny is the smallest unit, denying even one of them denies everything, and that is how the word became a way of saying total lack.
senses.whyCN: 一便士是最小单位，连一枚都否认就等于否认全部，这个词便由此成了「完全没有」的说法。

intro.en: Penny is an old Germanic word for a small coin; its deeper origin is uncertain, and it has no reliable Latin relative.
intro.cn: penny 是日耳曼语中表示小硬币的古老词，更早的来源不确定，也没有可靠的拉丁同族词。

items.en: A reconstructed form for a small coin; the exact meaning and origin of the stem are uncertain.
items.cn: 这是重构出来的「小硬币」形式；词干的确切含义与来源都不确定。

items.en: Old English had penig and pening for a penny, a coin and a unit of account.
items.cn: 古英语写作 penig 或 pening，既指硬币，也指记账单位。

items.en: Middle English simplified the spelling to peni and used penies as the regular plural.
items.cn: 中古英语把拼写简化为 peni，并用 penies 作规则复数。

items.en: Speakers split the plural in two: pence for an amount of money, pennies for separate coins.
items.cn: 使用者把复数一分为二：pence 指金额，pennies 指一枚枚硬币。

items.en: Decimal coinage from 1971 kept the penny, and American English uses the same word for its one-cent coin.
items.cn: 一九七一年起的十进制币制保留了 penny，美式英语也用同一个词指一分硬币。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the plural forms, derived words and compounds of the coin name; the near-meaning group collects other small units of money.
note.cn: 形近组收这枚硬币名称的复数形式、派生词与复合词；近义组收其他小额货币单位。

entries.definition: The plural used when a penny is counted as an amount of money.
entries.definitionCN: 把便士当作金额计算时使用的复数。

entries.definition: Having no money at all.
A former British coin worth six old pennies.
entries.definitionCN: 英国旧时值六便士的硬币。

entries.definition: A former British coin worth half a penny.
entries.definitionCN: 英国旧时值半便士的硬币。

entries.definition: A unit of money worth one hundredth of a dollar.
entries.definitionCN: 等于一美元百分之一的货币单位。

entries.definition: A piece of metal money.
Coins of low value returned or kept after paying.
entries.definitionCN: 付款后找回或留下的零钱。

entries.definition: British informal for a coin of low value.
entries.definitionCN: 英式口语，指低面值的铜币。

normalIntro.en: The word is an old coin name with two plurals, and its family grows through English compounds and suffixes rather than Latin parts.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是古老的硬币名，带着两个复数；同族词靠英语的复合与后缀生长，而不是拉丁部件。

normal.en: Old English penig is the direct ancestor, and the spelling changed but the small coin stayed.
normal.cn: 古英语 penig 是直系祖先，拼写变了，小硬币的意思没变。

normal.en: Pence answers how much, pennies answers how many pieces, which is why a price list never says pennies.
normal.cn: pence 回答「多少钱」，pennies 回答「几枚」，所以价目表从不写 pennies。

normal.en: The suffix -less in penniless means without, so the word simply says without a penny.
normal.cn: penniless 里的后缀 -less 意为「没有」，所以这个词就是「没有一便士」。

normal.en: A penny-pinching person pinches every penny until it hurts, and the compound names the habit.
normal.cn: penny-pinching 的人把每一分钱都攥到发疼，这个复合词命名的正是这种习惯。

normal.en: A penny for your thoughts asks for a thought as if it were worth one small coin.
normal.cn: a penny for your thoughts 把你的想法当作只值一枚小硬币来索要。

abstract.en: A coin small enough to lose is also small enough to stand for every coin you do not have.
abstract.cn: 小到容易丢失的一枚硬币，也小到能代表你缺的每一分钱。

abstract.en: One word holding two plurals is a small lesson in how English separates the thing from its value.
abstract.cn: 一个词带着两个复数，正好说明英语如何把「东西」和「价值」分开。

abstract.en: The penny survives because a price needs a smallest step, and a language needs a word for almost nothing.
abstract.cn: penny 能留下来，因为价格需要一个最小刻度，语言也需要一个表示「几乎没有」的词。

examples.en: The newspaper costs two pounds and fifty pence.
examples.cn: 这份报纸卖两英镑五十便士。

examples.en: He emptied his pockets and counted the pennies.
examples.cn: 他把口袋掏空，数着一枚枚便士。

examples.en: She never spends a penny on herself.
examples.cn: 她从不为自己花一分钱。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「喷你」——喷泉边掉出一枚小硬币，水花喷你一身；记住 penny 是便士、小硬币。

root: 古英语 penig、pening，可上溯到原始日耳曼语的重构形式 *panninga-；更早来源不确定，一般认为与拉丁语没有可靠的同族关系。

sensesIntro.en: The word names a coin, its value and its smallest-amount use; the two plurals carry the split between pieces and amounts.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词既指硬币、又指币值，还用于「一分钱」；两个复数分别承担「一枚枚」和「金额」的分工。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a worn copper disc lying in an open palm.
core.cn: 核心意象：一枚磨得发亮的铜色小圆片躺在掌心。

branches.en: a price tag reading fifty pence
branches.cn: 价签上写着五十便士

branches.en: a child counting coins into a jar
branches.cn: 孩子把硬币数进罐子

branches.en: a vending machine taking one-cent coins
branches.cn: 售货机收下一分硬币

branches.en: an empty pocket turned inside out
branches.cn: 翻过来的空口袋

branches.en: from a stated amount to a total lack
branches.cn: 从标明的金额到彻底没有

intro.en: The word is Germanic, so its building blocks are the old coin name plus English endings and compounds rather than Latin parts.
intro.cn: 这个词属日耳曼语，所以它的构件是古老的硬币名，加上英语后缀与复合词，而不是拉丁部件。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word; the early coin name is Germanic and its deeper origin is uncertain.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录；早期的硬币名属日耳曼语，更早的来源不确定。

items.meaningCN: 表示金额时使用的复数
